findings.title: `init()` timeout supply is contradictory between Task 15 and Task 17
findings.description: Task 15's first bullet gives the signature `init(operationPath: string)` and says it runs the submodule update "with `{ timeoutMs: GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS }`" — i.e. the timeout is built into `init()`. Its second bullet then says `sync()` must call `init()` "without the timeout: pass the timeout as an `init()` option so `sync()` and `update()` keep unbounded behavior (D10)" — i.e. the timeout is opt-in via a parameter. These cannot both hold: if `init()` applies the constant internally, `sync()` inherits the bound and D10's "install/update stay unbounded" is violated; if the timeout is opt-in, no task says who passes `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS` — Task 17's `ensureCheckout()` steps (line 249) never mention supplying it, so a literal implementation leaves auto-init unbounded, the exact hang D10/F004 was raised to close. Pin one shape (e.g. `init(operationPath, opts?: { timeoutMs?: number })` with `ensureCheckout()` passing `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS`) and name the supplying caller in Task 17.

findings.title: Config-file alias deprecation warning is implemented but never tested
findings.description: The slice design's functional success criterion (925-slice…md:193) requires: "A project whose shared config has `guide.git_strategy: manual` installs as tarball with the same warning." Task 7's second bullet implements the print (`guidesInstallAction()` emits the config-path deprecation warning from Task 5's return shape), but no test asserts it: Task 6(b) only checks that the manager reports the alias, and Task 8's CLI cases cover only the `--strategy manual` flag path, not the config-sourced path's stderr output. Add one case to Task 8 (config with `guide.git_strategy: manual`, no flag → deprecation line on stderr) so the criterion is verified end-to-end.

findings.title: Commit directives live inside checklist items instead of plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: The file has no `**Commit**:` markers as such; commit messages are embedded in the "Success criteria" checkbox text (lines 100, 127, 153, 204, 224, 246, 276, 312, 333, 342, 373, 389, 412). The placements themselves are correct — each sits at a working, tested point after the paired test task passes, not after every task and not only at the end — so this is purely a format note: extracting them as plain `**Commit**:` lines would match the convention and keep them out of checklist items the task-checker ticks off. Absence of markers is acceptable; no action strictly required.

findings.title: Task 10 is not independently completable as written
findings.description: Task 10's own success criterion is "typecheck passes once Task 11 populates the field" — i.e. its completion depends on a later task. Adding a required `checkout: SubmoduleCheckoutState | null` field to `GuideInfo` will break existing constructors until Task 11 (or an interim `checkout: null` fill) lands. Either make the field optional in Task 10 and narrow it in Task 11, or merge Tasks 10–11 into one task; as-is the pair is fine in sequence but Task 10 alone cannot reach its stated success state.

findings.title: Success criteria coverage is complete
findings.description: All ten functional criteria map to tasks: fresh-clone `cf build` + stderr SHA notice and clean `--json` stdout (Task 21); read-only `cf guides info` reporting "Checkout: not initialized" (Tasks 12, 24, with directory-unchanged assertions); out-of-sync warning without mutation (Tasks 18, 21); `--strategy manual` alias + `Method: tarball` output (Tasks 7, 8); config alias install (Tasks 5–7, subject to the test gap above); `cf init --strategy tarball` with no `.gitmodules` (Task 27); both `--help` outputs listing three strategies (Tasks 25–27); managed-directory line and README parity (Tasks 28–30); malformed config failing explicitly (Tasks 5, 6c). Technical criteria are likewise covered (real-git submodule fixture Tasks 9/12, `ensureCheckout` branch tests Task 18, `normalizeGuideMethod` rejection cases Task 2, the two grep-based literal checks in Tasks 3/5/7 and re-verified in Task 32, CHANGELOG/DEVLOG Task 31). The slice restates no NFR (F006 explicitly closed), so no `tests/load/` task or CI gating is required. Sequencing respects dependencies throughout: the fixture (Task 9) precedes every consumer, `gitExec` timeout (13–14) precedes `init()` (15–16), and `ensureCheckout` (17–18) precedes all call-site wiring (19–23). No scope creep found; Task 20's added `PROMPT_FILE_RELATIVE_PATH` grep is a completeness fix to the design's call-site enumeration, not extra scope.
